text_blocks.snippet: Early signs of type 2 diabetes develop slowly and often go unnoticed for years.
You can learn more about the condition and its indicators through the Mayo Clinic Type 2 Diabetes Guide.

list.snippet: Increased thirst and frequent urination: High blood sugar forces your kidneys to work harder to remove extra sugar, making you pee more often and feel very thirsty.
Constant fatigue: Your body cannot use sugar properly for energy, leaving you feeling tired even after resting.
Blurred vision: Extra sugar in your blood can change the fluid levels and shape of the lens in your eye.
Slow-healing cuts and sores: High blood sugar affects blood flow and nerve function, making minor wounds take much longer to heal.
Frequent infections: Skin, yeast, or bladder infections happen more often because bacteria and yeast thrive on excess sugar.
Tingling or numbness: Nerve irritation can cause a prickly feeling or loss of sensation in your hands or feet.
Darkened skin patches: Velvety dark skin, known as acanthosis nigricans, often appears on the neck or armpits and signals insulin resistance.
